definition: Learning a policy purely from a fixed dataset of past trajectories, with no environment interaction.
details: Learning a policy purely from a fixed dataset of past trajectories, with no environment interaction. Attractive wherever exploration is expensive or unsafe; the core difficulty is avoiding overestimating actions the data never tried.

explainer.lead: Offline RL learns a policy purely from a fixed dataset of past trajectories, with no environment interaction. It is attractive wherever exploration is expensive or unsafe.

tiers.eli5: Like learning to drive only from recordings of other people's trips, with no chance to practice yourself.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fit policies to logged trajectories so they can improve behaviour without risky trial and error in the real environment. The core pitfall is overestimating actions the data never tried.
tiers.paperLevel: A policy is learned from a fixed dataset of past trajectories without environment interaction. A known limit is overestimation of the value of actions absent from the data.

explainer.example: A policy for a physical system is trained from previously logged trajectories, avoiding live experimentation on the equipment.
